arxiv-2102-05634.title: Almost Robinson geometries Thanks: Funding. AF was supported by GNSAGA of INdAM, by PRIN 2017 “Real and Complex Manifolds: Topology, Geometry and Holomorphic Dynamics" and by a grant from the Simons Foundation (#944448). TL was supported by the Australian Research Council (Discovery Program DP190102
arxiv-2102-05634.creator: Anna Fino, Thomas Leistner, Arman Taghavi-Chabert ∗
arxiv-2102-05634.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Anna Fino, Thomas Leistner, Arman Taghavi-Chabert ∗. We investigate the geometry of almost Robinson manifolds, Lorentzian analogues of almost Hermitian manifolds, defined by Nurowski and Trautman as Lorentzian manifolds of even dimension equipped with a totally null complex distribution of maximal rank. Associated to such a structure, there is a congruence of null curves, which, in dimension four, is geodesic and non-shearing if and only if the complex distribution is involutive.

arxiv-2107-10066.title: Adaptive Inducing Points Selection for Gaussian Processes
arxiv-2107-10066.creator: Théo Galy-Fajou, Manfred Opper
arxiv-2107-10066.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Théo Galy-Fajou, Manfred Opper. Gaussian Processes ( GPs ) are flexible non-parametric models with strong probabilistic interpretation. While being a standard choice for performing inference on time series, GPs have little techniques to work in a streaming setting. 2017 ) developed an efficient variational approach to train online GPs by using sparsity techniques: The whole set of observations is approximated by a smaller set of inducing points ( IPs ) and moved around with new data.

arxiv-2109-12761.title: OpenViDial 2.0: A Larger-Scale, Open-Domain Dialogue Generation Dataset with Visual Contexts
arxiv-2109-12761.creator: Shuhe Wang, Yuxian Meng, Xiaoya Li, Xiaofei Sun, Rongbin Ouyang Jiwei Li
arxiv-2109-12761.description: Abstract In order to better simulate the real human conversation process, models need to generate dialogue utterances based on not only preceding textual contexts but also visual contexts. However, with the development of multi-modal dialogue learning, the dataset scale gradually becomes a bottleneck. In this report, we release OpenViDial 2.

arxiv-2111-06789.title: Lipschitz Carnot-Carathéodory structures and their limits
arxiv-2111-06789.creator: Gioacchino Antonelli, Enrico Le Donne, Sebastiano Nicolussi Golo
arxiv-2111-06789.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Gioacchino Antonelli, Enrico Le Donne, Sebastiano Nicolussi Golo. In this paper we discuss the convergence of distances associated to converging structures of Lipschitz vector fields and continuously varying norms on a smooth manifold. We prove that, under a mild controllability assumption on the limit vector-fields structure, the distances associated to equi-Lipschitz vector-fields structures that converge uniformly on compact subsets, and to norms that converge uniformly on compact subsets, converge locally uniformly to the limit Carnot-Carathéodory distance.

arxiv-2112-08252.title: Sampling rare trajectories using stochastic bridges
arxiv-2112-08252.creator: Javier Aguilar, Joseph W. Baron, Tobias Galla, Raúl Toral
arxiv-2112-08252.description: Abstract The numerical quantification of the statistics of rare events in stochastic processes is a challenging computational problem. We present a sampling method that constructs an ensemble of stochastic trajectories that are constrained to have fixed start and end points (so-called stochastic bridges).

arxiv-2310-04458.title: Simultaneous Dimensionality Reduction: A Data Efficient Approach for Multimodal Representations Learning
arxiv-2310-04458.creator: Eslam Abdelaleem eslam.abdelaleem@emory.edu, Ahmed Roman ahmed.hemdan.roman@emory.edu, K. Michael Martini karl.michael.martini@emory.edu, Ilya Nemenman ilya.nemenman@emory.edu
arxiv-2310-04458.description: Abstract Current experiments frequently produce high-dimensional, multimodal datasets—such as those combining neural activity and animal behavior or gene expression and phenotypic profiling—with the goal of extracting useful correlations between the modalities. Often, the first step in analyzing such datasets is dimensionality reduction.

arxiv-2311-05229.title: Mean Field Games in a Stackelberg problem with an informed major player
arxiv-2311-05229.creator: Philippe Bergault, Pierre Cardaliaguet, Catherine Rainer
arxiv-2311-05229.description: Abstract We investigate a stochastic differential game in which a major player has a private information (the knowledge of a random variable), which she discloses through her control to a population of small players playing in a Nash Mean Field Game equilibrium.

arxiv-2505-21330.title: UGCE: User-Guided Incremental Counterfactual Exploration Thanks: This paper has been accepted to the ForgtAI Workshop at IJCNN 2025.
arxiv-2505-21330.creator: Christos Fragkathoulas, Evaggelia Pitoura
arxiv-2505-21330.description: Abstract Counterfactual explanations (CFEs) are a popular approach for interpreting machine learning predictions by identifying minimal feature changes that alter model outputs. However, in real-world settings, users often refine feasibility constraints over time, requiring counterfactual generation to adapt dynamically. Existing methods fail to support such iterative updates, instead recomputing explanations from scratch with each change, an inefficient and rigid approach.

pmc-12647998.title: A promising novel local anesthetic for effective anesthesia in oral inflammatory conditions through reducing mitochondria-related apoptosis
pmc-12647998.creator: Haofan Wang, Yihang Hao, Wenrui Gai, Shilong Hu, Wencheng Liu, Bo Ma, Rongjia Shi, Yongzhen Tan, Ting Kang, Ao Hai, Yi Zhao, Yaling Tang, Ling Ye, Jin Liu, Xinhua Liang, Bowen Ke
pmc-12647998.description: Local anesthetics (LAs), such as articaine (AT), exhibit limited efficacy in inflammatory environments, which constitutes a significant limitation in their clinical application within oral medicine. In our prior research, we developed AT-17, which demonstrated effective properties in chronic inflammatory conditions and appears to function as a novel oral LA that could address this challenge.

pmc-13336589.title: Emerging topical nonsteroidal therapies in pediatric dermatology: atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, alopecia areata, vitiligo, and seborrheic dermatitis
pmc-13336589.creator: Jordan Gillespie, Tracy Funk, Julie Dhossche, Liza Kenny, Alison Small
pmc-13336589.description: Purpose of reviewTo review the current literature for updates on pediatric nonsteroidal topical therapies (NSTT) for the treatment of atopic dermatitis (AD), psoriasis, alopecia areata (AA), vitiligo, and seborrheic dermatitis (SD).Recent findingsThe FDA approved difamilast and expanded the approved age ranges for roflumilast, tapinarof, and ruxolitinib to treat AD. Recent studies also show positive results with delgocitinib.

pmc-13691556.title: ESTRO-EPTN guidelines for independent dose calculation and log file-based patient-specific quality assurance in scanned particle therapy
pmc-13691556.creator: Loïc Grevillot, Oliver Jäkel, Abdallah Qubala, Julian Horn, Adam H. Aitkenhead, Xiaoying Liang, Giuseppe Magro, Klará Badraoui-Čuprová, Jan Vilimovský, Jörg Wulff, Katrin Henkner, Catharine H. Clark, Damir Skrijelj, Ilaria Rinaldi, Kevin Souris, Séverine Rossomme, Franciska Lebbink, Liu Hong, Dawid
pmc-13691556.description: Background and Purpose: Independent dose calculation (IDC) and log file-based patient-specific quality assurance (PSQA) are increasingly used in scanned particle therapy (PT) to address pitfalls of phantom-based verifications. Highly modulated treatment fields, steep dose gradients, and growing interest for adaptive treatments require quality assurance (QA) approaches that are cost effective, patient-specific, and closely linked to the delivered treatment.
